children: Outdoor specialty retailer's Q2 revenue rose 0.6% yr/yr; same-store sales were flat
Q2 adjusted net loss and adjusted loss per share narrowed from prior year
Company cut inventory by $44.5 mln and net debt by $26 mln yr/yr
Sportsman's Warehouse reaffirms 2026 same store sales guidance of down 1.0% to up 2.0%
Company expects 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $30 mln to $36 mln
Sportsman's Warehouse expects 2026 capital expenditures of $20 mln to $25 mln, with no new store openings
HUNTING AND SHOOTING SPORTS - Co said 6.7% growth in Hunting and Shooting Sports, led by firearms and ammunition, helped offset declines in other categories
INVENTORY MANAGEMENT - Gross margin improvement attributed to more disciplined inventory management reducing freight expense and a one-time tariff benefit
CONSUMER AND WEATHER PRESSURE - Declines in other categories reflected continued pressure on U.S. consumer and drought conditions in western U.S. impacting fishing sales
*Applies to a deviation of less than 1%; not applicable for per-share numbers.
The current average analyst rating on the shares is "buy" and the breakdown of recommendations is 3 "strong buy" or "buy", no "hold" and no "sell" or "strong sell"
The average consensus recommendation for the miscellaneous specialty retailers peer group is "buy"
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Sportsman's Warehouse Holdings Inc is $3.00, about 152.1% above its August 31 closing price of $1.19
Sept 1 - US job openings rise in July after sharp downward revision in prior month
